question: Will a division (bloc vote) be held on Malaysia's Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on 26 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: final committee-stage/third-reading sittings of Malaysian budgets under the Anwar government (Budgets 2024, 2025, 2026). All passed by voice vote with no recorded division found in reporting; the only recent budget division was PN forcing one at Budget 2026's policy stage. For Budget 2027 PN did not even call a division at the policy stage despite having >15 MPs and an obvious motive (CSA signatories), and every committee-stage allocation so far has passed by voice vote. Upside: final day is a natural symbolic moment (Finance Ministry allocation/third reading), and political friction (Najib pardon, Melaka election, early-GE talk) could provoke a show vote. No human prediction market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers: none).
calls.dossier:
- Budget 2026 (Supply Bill 2026): policy stage 4 Nov 2025 passed by division forced by PN chief whip Takiyuddin, 120-67, 35 absent (The Edge node/777531). Third reading 1 Dec 2025 passed by voice vote (The Star 2025-12-01; The Edge node/784289). Committee-stage allocations reported passed by voice vote throughout Nov 2025 (Malay Mail 2025-11-11, 2025-11-21; Bernama).
- Budget 2025: committee stage and third reading passed by voice vote (The Edge node/736437, Dec 2024).
- Budget 2024: passed by voice vote 27 Nov 2023 (Malay Mail 2023-11-27); policy stage also voice vote (The Edge node/688670).
- Budget 2021 (Dec 2020, Muhyiddin govt, thin majority): third reading passed by division 111-108; committee-stage divisions also occurred. Different regime (razor-thin majority).
- Budget 2027: policy stage 29 Oct 2026 passed by voice vote, no division called, hours after CSA with 13 MPs (Malaysiakini 888129; The Star 2026-10-29). Govt reportedly has 147 of 222.
- Committee stage 2-26 Nov 2026; as of week 6 (to 13 Nov), allocations for approved ministries all passed by voice vote; 16 ministries remain (Bernama id=2633670).
- Division needs 15 MPs standing; PN (PAS + remaining Bersatu) has far more than 15 MPs; PN refused to sign CSA.
- Senator Ahmad Ibrahim (15 Nov 2026) confirms Dewan Rakyat to complete committee stage 26 Nov; Dewan Negara from 30 Nov.
- Status quo: final budget sitting concludes with voice votes on final allocations and third reading.
- Base rates: over Anwar-era budgets 2024-2026 final-day/third-reading divisions: 0 of 3 found. Over budget policy stages 2024-2027: 1 of 4 had a division (2026). Over all stages of Budget 2027 so far: 0 divisions.
- Resolves off official Hansard (Penyata Rasmi) for 26 Nov 2026 sitting; division must be on the Supply Bill 2027 (committee allocation or third reading), before 20:00 UTC (04:00 MYT 27 Nov).
- Event window: 26 Nov 2026 00:00 UTC -> 20:00 UTC; as of 16 Nov 2026 0% elapsed.
- Searched, absent: any PN statement on intent to call a division at committee stage/third reading of Budget 2027; Hansard-level confirmation of zero committee-stage divisions in 2023-2025 (news reports only); any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: Final-day committee stage / third reading of Malaysian Supply Bills 2023-2025 (Budgets 2024-2026)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: final committee-stage day and third reading of Malaysian budgets under the unity government (Budget 2023 to 2026). The third readings I checked (Budget 2025, Budget 2026) passed by voice vote, and none of these closing days had a division that I could find. For Budget 2026, PN forced a division only at policy stage, not at committee stage or third reading. For Budget 2027, PN did not even call one at policy stage, which came hours after the CSA brought the government to 147 MPs, and BN and PN cooperated in Melaka. Upside risks: PN may want to put the CSA signatories on record, plus talk of an early election and UMNO-DAP friction. In 2020, under a thin majority, there were many committee-stage divisions. No prediction market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers).
calls.dossier:
- Budget 2026: policy stage on 4 Nov 2025 passed by division (120-67, 35 absent) after PN chief whip Takiyuddin called for it (The Edge, Bharian). On the same day, the PMD, Finance and Foreign Ministry allocations passed at committee stage, apparently without a division. The third reading on 1 Dec 2025 passed by majority voice vote (The Star, 1 Dec 2025).
- Budget 2025: policy stage on 12 Nov 2024 passed by voice vote. The third reading on 3 Dec 2024 passed by voice vote (The Edge, FMT).
- No reports found of committee-stage divisions in the Budget 2024-2026 cycles (searched, absent).
- Contrast: Budget 2021 (Dec 2020, PN government with a thin majority): 9 of 27 ministries went to division at committee stage (Kosmo/Utusan, Dec 2020). A division needs 15+ MPs standing.
- Budget 2027: policy stage on 29 Oct 2026 passed by voice vote with no division called, hours after the CSA with 13 MPs (6 Bersatu incl. Muhyiddin, Syed Saddiq, 6 ex-Bersatu). Government at 147/222.
- Committee stage runs 2-26 Nov 2026. By 13 Nov, four ministries (NRES, Higher Education, Domestic Trade, Home) were reported approved and 16 ministries remained; no division reported (Malay Mail, Bernama).
- PN refused to sign the CSA. BN and PN cooperated in the 14 Nov 2026 Melaka state election (Takiyuddin, FMT 14 Nov 2026). There is talk of early dissolution and UMNO-DAP friction over Najib.
- Third reading expected at the end of the 26 Nov sitting, which may run late. The Dewan Negara starts on 30 Nov.
- Status quo: closing days of budgets in the unity-government era ended by voice vote.
- Resolves off the Hansard of the 26 Nov sitting: a division on a Supply Bill 2027 committee allocation or the third reading, 08:00 MYT 26 Nov to 04:00 MYT 27 Nov.
- Event window: 26 Nov 00:00 UTC -> 26 Nov 20:00 UTC. As of 16 Nov 2026, 0% elapsed.
- Searched for and not found: any PN statement planning a division on Budget 2027; a prediction market.
calls.reference_class: Final committee-stage day / third reading of Malaysian Supply Bills, 2023-2025 unity-government era (with the 2020 thin-majority era as a contrasting class)

calls.reasoning: Under the Anwar unity government, the committee stage and third reading of Budgets 2024, 2025 and 2026 all passed by voice vote. That includes Budget 2026, where PN forced a division only at the policy stage. For Budget 2027, PN did not even call a division at the policy stage. Upside risk: PN may want to put the CSA signatories on record, it easily meets the 15-MP threshold, and anger over the CSA is high. Downside: in 2024 and 2025 the third reading fell on a later day, after committee stage ended, which would push any third-reading division outside the window. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- Budget 2026 (2025 cycle): policy stage passed by division on 4 Nov 2025 (120-67, 35 absent) after PN called it. Committee-stage allocations were passed by voice vote (Malay Mail, 11 Nov 2025). Committee stage ran to 27 Nov, but the third reading was on 1 Dec 2025 by voice vote (The Star, 1 Dec 2025).
- Budget 2025 (2024 cycle): committee-stage allocations passed by majority voice vote (Bernama weekly review, Nov 2024). Third reading on 3 Dec 2024 by voice vote (FMT, 3 Dec 2024).
- Budget 2024 (2023 cycle): policy stage passed by voice vote on 2 Nov 2023. Committee stage and third reading passed by voice vote on 27 Nov 2023 (Malaysiakini, Nov 2023).
- Budget 2021 (Dec 2020, PN government with a thin majority): the PH opposition called about 8+ committee-stage divisions plus a third-reading division (111-108). This shows divisions are common when the opposition is contesting the majority (Malaysiakini, Dec 2020).
- Budget 2027: policy stage passed by voice vote on 29 Oct 2026, with no division called, hours after the CSA with 13 MPs was signed. The government has about 147 of 222 MPs. Suspended Bersatu MPs aligned with Hamzah were not invited to the CSA signing (Malaysiakini, Oct 2026).
- Committee stage is scheduled to end 26 Nov 2026 (Malay Mail, 16 Nov 2026). The Dewan Negara starts on 30 Nov, which implies the third reading must happen by about 26 Nov-early Dec, but its exact date is not confirmed. In 2024 and 2025 the third reading fell on a separate day after committee stage ended.
- A division requires 15 MPs to stand. PN has far more than 15 MPs.
- Status quo for the Anwar era: committee stage and third reading by voice vote (0 divisions found in the 2023-2025 cycles at those stages).
- Resolves off the Dewan Rakyat Hansard for 26 Nov 2026; only divisions on the Supply Bill count.
- Event window: 26 Nov 2026 00:00 UTC to 20:00 UTC (08:00 MYT 26 Nov to 04:00 MYT 27 Nov). As of 16 Nov 2026 12:30 UTC, 0% elapsed.
- Searched without finding: any PN statement on calling divisions during the Budget 2027 committee stage; a confirmed third-reading date; any committee-stage division in the 2023-2025 cycles; any prediction market (none on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: final committee-stage sittings and third readings of Anwar-era budgets (2024, 2025, 2026). All passed by voice vote, with no division reported. PN forced a division only at Budget 2026's policy stage. For Budget 2027, PN did not call one even at policy stage, after the CSA lifted the government to 147/222, and all committee allocations so far have passed by voice vote. Upside: PN easily has the 15 MPs needed, it has a motive to put CSA signatories on record, and early-election and UMNO-DAP friction could prompt a symbolic vote. Downside: the third reading may fall after 26 Nov, as it did in 2024 and 2025, which leaves only the final allocations inside the window. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the base facts: voice votes at the committee stage and third reading of Budgets 2024-2026, no Budget 2027 division so far, and no market found. One factual dispute could not be settled without web access: whether the third reading falls on 26 Nov. The question background says it is expected at the end of the 26 Nov sitting, but Run 3 notes the 2024 and 2025 third readings fell on later days. Even if it does fall later, the final allocations on 26 Nov stay in the window, so this dispute only trims the upside. Everything else was judgment: how much the CSA anger raises PN's appetite for a show vote. PN's silence at the policy stage is the strongest evidence against that. I take about 9%.

disagreements.claim: Third reading will occur within the 26 Nov window
disagreements.verdict: Unsettled: the background says 'expected' on 26 Nov, but the 2024/2025 precedent puts it on a later day. Carried as uncertainty that lowers the probability somewhat.

disagreements.claim: PN will use the final day to force CSA signatories on the record
disagreements.verdict: Unlikely given PN's silence at the policy stage and BN-PN cooperation in Melaka; kept as the main upside tail.

disagreements.claim: No committee-stage divisions occurred in the 2023-2025 cycles
disagreements.verdict: All three runs report none found in news coverage; accepted, though not confirmed at Hansard level.
